audits.title: Management of medically assisted withdrawal from alcohol in acute adult mental health and specialist addictions in-patient services: UK clinical audit findings
audits.standard: POMH audit standards for medically assisted alcohol withdrawal
audits.setting: Acute adult mental health wards/PICU and specialist NHS addictions units in 45 NHS mental health trusts (POMH national audit)

cycle1.result: 908 patients on acute wards/PICU and 347 in specialist addictions units; MAAW overseen by an addiction specialist in 33 (4%) of acute ward patients.

audits.other_findings: Alcohol history, breath alcohol, Wernicke's screening, parenteral thiamine, relapse-prevention prescribing and referral for continuing care were more often documented with specialist addictions involvement.
audits.citation: Sinclair J, Barnes T, Lingford-Hughes A, Drummond C, Loubser I, Rendora O, et al.. Management of medically assisted withdrawal from alcohol in acute adult mental health and specialist addictions in-patient services: UK clinical audit findings. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(3). doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.45.

audits.title: Audit on the Adherence to Guidelines for the Management of Alcohol Withdrawal Syndrome in a General Hospital
audits.standard: Health board policy NU16 for alcohol withdrawal syndrome management, based on NICE guidelines
audits.setting: Wards of Wrexham Maelor Hospital, general hospital

cycle1.result: Complete drinking history 4%; physical examination 84%; Wernicke's signs documented 20%; CIWA-Ar applied 44%, correctly scored 24%; benzodiazepines prescribed 38%; oral thiamine 58%; alcohol liaison opinion 16%.

audits.intervention: Training programmes on alcohol withdrawal management by the alcohol liaison team for all clinical staff.
audits.other_findings: Laboratory investigation compliance ranged from 16% for GGT to 84% for full blood count; 42% had IV Pabrinex two pairs three times daily.
audits.citation: Simiyon M, Connah R, Proffitt R, Downes S, Jarvis J, Baker C. Audit on the Adherence to Guidelines for the Management of Alcohol Withdrawal Syndrome in a General Hospital. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S177-S178. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.464.

audits.title: Improving Acute Treatment of Alcohol Withdrawal at an Inpatient De-addiction Ward (‘Vimukthi’) at Kerala State, India: Full Cycle of a Clinical Audit
audits.standard: ASAM, NICE and Government of India guidelines: long-acting benzodiazepines with fixed-dose, symptom-triggered or front-loading regimens according to setting and risk
audits.setting: Dedicated 10-bed inpatient de-addiction ward ('Vimukthi') attached to a general hospital, Kerala

cycle1.result: Fixed-dose regimen of short-acting lorazepam used for all patients; no documentation of risk profiling.

audits.intervention: Standard operating procedure with risk profiling, symptom-triggered regimen using nurse-administered CIWA-Ar and front-loading for high risk, introduced after team discussion and training in October 2023.

cycle2.result: Risk stratification documented (34% low, 52% intermediate, 14% high risk); symptom-triggered regimen given to all patients with front-loading for all high-risk patients; oral lorazepam fell from 3324 mg for 63 patients (Oct–Dec 2022) to 10 mg for 39 patients.

audits.other_findings: Injectable lorazepam use rose by 25% (0.8 mg to 1 mg per patient) and oral diazepam rose from nil to 170 mg. Staff and patients reported satisfaction with the new protocol.
audits.citation: S A, Kuriakose A, Sathiaseelan R. Improving Acute Treatment of Alcohol Withdrawal at an Inpatient De-addiction Ward (‘Vimukthi’) at Kerala State, India: Full Cycle of a Clinical Audit. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S14-S15. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.100.

audits.title: Prescribing for Substance Misuse: Alcohol Detoxification in Adult Mental Health Inpatient Services. The National Prescribing Observatory for Mental Health (POMH-UK) Quality Improvement Programme: 14c
audits.standard: POMH-UK Quality Improvement Programme 14c: 5 standards (12 criteria) and 3 targets for alcohol detoxification
audits.setting: Acute adult, PICU and specialist inpatient units across 4 boroughs (Warrington, Halton, Knowsley, Wigan), Mersey Care Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Four of twelve criteria (liver function and glucose tests, prescription for acute withdrawal, parenteral thiamine) and all three targets (breath test at admission, relapse prevention, referral to specialist alcohol services) had less than 60% compliance and were below the national sample.

audits.intervention: Recommended trust-wide guidance, a junior doctor admission checklist, induction teaching and routine admission bloods.
audits.other_findings: Second re-audit in the POMH-UK cycle, compared with 2016; practice varied across the trust.
audits.citation: Anwar F, Siddiq H, Nuttall R. Prescribing for Substance Misuse: Alcohol Detoxification in Adult Mental Health Inpatient Services. The National Prescribing Observatory for Mental Health (POMH-UK) Quality Improvement Programme: 14c. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S217-S218. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10550.

audits.title: Clinical Audit of Physical Examinations and Cognitive Assessments for Patients on Alcohol Detoxification, in Bridge House Detoxification Unit
audits.standard: NICE guidelines and Trust policy: physical examination on admission and cognitive assessment before discharge
audits.setting: Bridge House inpatient alcohol detoxification unit

cycle1.result: Physical examination done in 98%; cognitive assessment before discharge in 7%.

audits.other_findings: About 30% had cognitive assessment in the admission plan but it was not actioned before discharge; mean stay about 14 days.
audits.citation: Fatunla S. Clinical Audit of Physical Examinations and Cognitive Assessments for Patients on Alcohol Detoxification, in Bridge House Detoxification Unit. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S235-S235. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10587.

audits.title: A Quality Improvement (QI) Project to Improve Adherence to Alcohol Dependence Guidelines in an Acute Adult Inpatient Setting
audits.standard: Trust Alcohol Dependence Guidelines for assessment and management of alcohol withdrawal
audits.setting: Cedar ward, acute adult psychiatric inpatient unit, Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: SADQ/weekly alcohol intake documented in 44.4%; regular chlordiazepoxide prescribed per guideline in 55.6% (lower for as-required); escalation for clinical review documented in 25%; CIWA-Ar completed in 23.97%.

audits.intervention: Teaching for nursing staff and resident doctors, alcohol-withdrawal guidance in nursing induction, electronic prescribing prompts for CIWA-Ar, CIWA-Ar and SADQ tools in the electronic record, and guideline review with the Area Prescribing Committee, via PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Authors report improved clinician confidence, recognition and documentation of withdrawal symptoms; no figures given.

audits.other_findings: A resident doctor survey found gaps in awareness and process problems on the ward.
audits.citation: Tum A, Senanayake S, Arikan A, Krishnan D, Rajendram M. A Quality Improvement (QI) Project to Improve Adherence to Alcohol Dependence Guidelines in an Acute Adult Inpatient Setting. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S210-S210. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11504.

audits.title: A Re-Audit of the Assessment and Management of Alcohol Misuse Following Admission to the General Adult Inpatient Wards in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
audits.standard: Trust alcohol detoxification policy and NICE guidance
audits.setting: Eight general adult psychiatric inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: CIWA score documented within 24 hours in 1% of patients with alcohol misuse.

cycle2.result: Alcohol history documented on admission in 55%; weekly intake recorded in 28% of those with prior misuse; CIWA within 24 hours 17%; chlordiazepoxide started in 14%, thiamine 25%, Vitamin B Compound Strong 3%; gamma GT 31%, Mg2+ 25%; 0% offered referral to community alcohol services.

audits.other_findings: A 2022 re-audit showed CIWA within 24 hours in 4%. Referral to community alcohol services worsened compared with earlier audits; clerking proformas and targeted education were recommended.
audits.citation: Wilson J, Rigby E, Hyland D. A Re-Audit of the Assessment and Management of Alcohol Misuse Following Admission to the General Adult Inpatient Wards in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S302-S303. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11699.

audits.title: Initial Assessment of Alcohol-Related Psychiatric Admissions: A Clinical Audit From Malta
audits.standard: American Society of Addiction Medicine Clinical Practice Guideline for Alcohol Withdrawal Management
audits.setting: Acute psychiatric inpatient service, Mount Carmel Hospital

cycle1.result: Alcohol use documented in 132 (70%); of 36 regular drinkers, duration of dependency and time of last drink documented in 8.3%, CIWA-A in 66.7%, previous withdrawal delirium, seizures and autonomic activation 0%; urine toxicology 63.9%, LFTs 52.8%, INR 27.8%, ethanol 36.11%.

audits.intervention: Recommended a locally adapted alcohol assessment guideline and re-audit.
audits.other_findings: Comorbidities (100%), other substance use (100%) and suicide risk (91.7%) were well documented.
audits.citation: Pace E, Scicluna S, Camilleri E. Initial Assessment of Alcohol-Related Psychiatric Admissions: A Clinical Audit From Malta. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S293-S293. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11720.
